newsitem.title: USA: FCOJ futures end down after USDA Florida crop data.
newsitem.headline: FCOJ futures end down after USDA Florida crop data.

text.p: NYCE frozen concentrated orange juice futures closed lower following the U.S. Department of Agriculture's first estimate for the 1996/97 Florida orange crop.
Floor sources cited speculative, local selling, and late-session fund selling, while the trade was on both sides of the market.
The USDA put the crop at 220 million boxes, towards the high end of expectations which ranged from 215 million to 225 million boxes. Last year's crop was 203.2 million boxes.

The estimate, coupled with continuously slack weekly movement data, was enough to pressure the deferred contracts to lifetime lows. January fell to a low of 102.10 but spot November did not slip under its lifetime low of 103.00, made September 5.
"(Today's weakness) was partially due to the report because it came in at the upper end of the range. But to top it off, we had a very poor (weekly) movement yesterday," an analyst said.
November closed 0.95 lower at 111.25, having ranged from 111.50 to 107.50. The back months ended 3.10 to 2.25 weaker.
Support in November was seen at 107.00 and then 105.00, while resistance remained between 115.00 and 116.00.
